questions.q: Why does MySQL need the DELIMITER trick when defining a stored procedure?
options: Because the procedure body itself contains ordinary semicolons, which would otherwise be read as the end of the whole CREATE PROCEDURE statement
Because MySQL requires a special character before every statement
Because DELIMITER changes the procedure's parameter types
Because MySQL doesn't support semicolons at all
questions.explain: DELIMITER // temporarily redefines the statement terminator so the client doesn't stop at the first semicolon inside the procedure body.

questions.q: Before PostgreSQL version 11, how did developers handle operations that were conceptually side-effecting procedures?
options: PostgreSQL never supported any form of stored routine before version 11
They used MySQL's DELIMITER trick instead
They built everything as FUNCTIONs, since CREATE PROCEDURE didn't exist yet
PostgreSQL has always had CREATE PROCEDURE since its first release
questions.explain: PostgreSQL only had CREATE FUNCTION until version 11 (2018) added a genuine CREATE PROCEDURE — before that, functions covered every use case, including side-effecting ones.

questions.q: What keyword do both MySQL and PostgreSQL use to invoke a stored procedure?
options: INVOKE
CALL
RUN
EXEC
questions.explain: Both platforms use CALL ProcName(...) to invoke a procedure, unlike T-SQL's EXEC.

questions.q: How does PostgreSQL spell the parameter direction that both receives and returns a value, compared to PL/SQL?
options: PostgreSQL spells it OUTIN
INOUT (one word) in PostgreSQL, vs. IN OUT (two words) in PL/SQL
Both platforms spell it identically as IN OUT
PostgreSQL has no equivalent to IN OUT
questions.explain: PostgreSQL procedures use the one-word INOUT, a small but real spelling difference from PL/SQL's two-word IN OUT.

questions.q: In the MySQL example, where does the procedure's OUT parameter value land when called?
options: In a MySQL session variable (e.g. @result_price), not a locally declared block variable
In a locally DECLAREd variable inside the same routine
MySQL cannot return output parameter values at all
It is automatically printed to the console with no variable needed
questions.explain: CALL GetProductPrice(707, @result_price) stores the OUT parameter's value in a MySQL session (user-defined) variable, which is readable afterward with SELECT @result_price.
